record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.context_brief: Triangles in three-space with three colors
record.original_question: For every triangle T, must every 3-coloring of Euclidean three-space E^3 contain a monochromatic congruent copy of T?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E^3$ denote three-dimensional Euclidean space. A coloring of $E^3$ with $r$ colors is a function $\chi: E^3 \to \{1, 2, \dots, r\}$. Given a finite point configuration $T \subset E^3$, we say a coloring $\chi$ contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$ if there exists an isometry $\sigma$ of $E^3$ such that $\chi$ is constant on $\sigma(T)$. Write $E^3 \to_r T$ to mean that every $r$-coloring of $E^3$ contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$.

Prove or disprove: for every (nondegenerate) triangle $T$ (i.e., every set of three non-collinear points in the plane, considered up to congruence), one has $E^3 \to_3 T$; that is, every $3$-coloring of $E^3$ contains three points forming a triangle congruent to $T$ all of the same color.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that every 3-coloring of $E^3$ contains a monochromatic congruent copy of any given triangle is a well-known open problem in Euclidean Ramsey theory, stated as a conjecture in surveys of open problems by Graham and collaborators. No proof or counterexample appears in the literature; only special cases and related planar/two-color statements have been studied.

status_evidence.title: Euclidean Ramsey Theorems. I — Graham, Straus et al.
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational paper on Euclidean Ramsey theory introducing the arrow notation E^n ->_r T and posing related conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: The problem fits within the standard Euclidean Ramsey framework and remains a stated conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Monochromatic triangle - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses conjectures about monochromatic congruent triangles under finite colorings of Euclidean space; several cases remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Related triangle Ramsey problems for Euclidean spaces are listed as open.
